COLLISION POINTS: the label on its own line, then one entry per line covering every defender link D1..Dn, none omitted. A link counted in w: D<i>: WITHDRAWN -- GROUND: <reason>; or, for a link withdrawn after an unanswered witness, D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): WITHDRAWN AFTER AN UNANSWERED WITNESS -- <grade> -- the grade counting as any collision grade. A link that a challenger link contradicts about the same text: D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN | CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN | UNDERDETERMINED -- one clause of why -- GROUND: <reason>; one such line per contradicting challenger link, and DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at most once per defender link. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the words of the layer of that answer that fails to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round>". Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A proven press (md_notes_rulings 398) that the broken side's later rounds left UNANSWERED is also a BROKEN ground (COUNTING RULE; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground). Grade UNDERDETERMINED only when the witnesses and the answers, read together, still leave the point open; an answer that names a witness without showing a fit does not leave the point open (md_notes_rulings 419). k is the number of lines graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN. A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. On every COLLISION POINTS line you grade DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, exhibit on that line itself at least two lower layers of DIFFERENT kinds, read by FOOTING LAYERS (md_notes_rulings 400). FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. A BROKEN line without them is a DEBATE RULE VIOLATION. The system checks every BROKEN line after you answer; a violating line is returned to you to cure, by exhibiting the two layers, or to answer in writing why it stands. An answer that does not exhibit them leaves the violation standing, and your judgment is then not counted. The same holds when your CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS count is 0 while you grade a link of that side BROKEN for a pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered. Both sides alike.

You are an adjudicator of a debate record. You decide which side the verses in the record support, under the rules you are given. You bring nothing from outside the record. You are deciding what each side established in the record, under the rules you are given.

### Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence.
The evidence is the rounds of both sides. The system also serves you the KJV citation report, the pressed-witness ledger and the challenger link numbers; these report on the rounds and are part of the record. The pre-checks are aids that decide nothing. Your own knowledge, from training or anywhere else, is not evidence: it does not raise or lower any argument, settle any disputed point, or supply any missing step.

### Commitment 2. I repair nothing.
You supply no missing step for either side. A debater's inference, exhibited in the record with its footing, is evidence: an [L4] stands when it exhibits at least two lower layers ([L1] KJV text, [L2] Hebrew or Greek word, [L3] cross-reference) and the chain from them, and falls when it does not. ### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words.
Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show, and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it.

### Commitment 4. One standard for both sides.
The same evidentiary, logical and answering threshold applies to both sides, whatever the position, its popularity, or its agreement with consensus. No side receives heightened scrutiny. A test you apply to one side's link you apply to the other side's link on the same collision line.

### Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral.
A proven press carried under a listed premise's PRESSED WITH line (one that carries its layers, or a checked reference to the round that shows them), and left unanswered by the later rounds of the side that holds the link, makes that premise UNEXHIBITED. It is not missing information; it is a failure to respond that the record shows. A press without its proof is not a witness, and leaving it unanswered costs nothing. A verse pressed with no listed premise behind it is not a witness. A premise carries at most eight witnesses.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** "Biological father" means a man who begot the child by his own seed. The KJV says that Joseph was not that man. The child was conceived in the virgin Mary by the Holy Ghost, "of a woman" alone on the human side. The Son of God was not begotten by a man.

---

## 1. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at the last link

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren." The same word is used for every father-to-son step down the line.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** *egennēsen* (G1080, "begat," the father's act of generating) is used in Matthew 1:2 and in the first half of Matthew 1:16. In the second half of Matthew 1:16 the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē* ("was born"), and the relative pronoun is *hēs* (G3739, "of whom"), which is feminine singular. It points to Mary alone, not to Joseph.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:16 does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." Joseph is called "the husband of Mary," and the birth is "of whom," the woman.

**[L4]** The footing is the unbroken *egennēsen* in Matthew 1:2 [L1/L2] and the feminine *hēs* in Matthew 1:16 [L2/L1]. The inference is that the evangelist keeps the father-begetting verb for every man in the line and withholds it from Joseph in the one case where the child is in view. He assigns the birth to Mary only.

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," and it came before Joseph and Mary came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537, G4151, G40: "out of Holy Spirit") names the source of the conception. *prin ē synelthein* ("before they came together") fixes the time as before any union. *en gastri echousa* ("having in womb") is the ordinary idiom for being with child.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew that he was not the father. He reasoned as a man who had not been with her, and the angel's word corrected his fear. It did not tell him the child was his.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The Greek verb *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know," here of marital knowledge) is negated up to the birth.

**[L4]** The footing is the declared source *ek pneumatos hagiou* [L2/L1 in Matthew 1:18 and 1:20] and the cross-reference that Joseph "knew her not" until the birth [L3, Matthew 1:25]. The inference is that the conception had a single stated source, the Holy Ghost, and no human male act was part of it.

## 3. Mary's own testimony and the angel's answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *andra* (G435, "a male human being, a man") and *ginōskō* (G1097, "know," marital sense). In Luke 1:34 the verb is present tense: "I know not." She had had no relation with any man.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *epeleusetai* (G1904, "shall come upon") and *episkiasei* (G1982, "shall overshadow") describe a divine act. *gennōmenon ek sou* ("born of thee") again names the woman as the source.

**[L3]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." The Hebrew *'almâh* (H5959) stands behind the KJV "virgin." Matthew 1:23 quotes it: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." The Greek *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") stands behind the KJV "virgin" there.

**[L4]** The footing is Mary's "I know not a man" [L1/L2] and the answer that the cause is "the Holy Ghost… the power of the Highest" [L1, Luke 1:35], read with the prophecy that a "virgin" conceives [L3, Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23]. The inference is that the answer to "How shall this be?" names God's power in place of a man's part. The conception had no biological contribution from a man.

## 4. Where Joseph is called father, the text marks it as supposition or as the speech of others

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, "was supposed, was reckoned by custom or opinion") marks a belief that was held but not true.

**[L1]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is the speech of the unbelieving crowd.

**[L3]** Luke 2:48–49: Mary says, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing," and the child answers, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child corrects who his Father is in the same exchange.

**[L4]** The footing is the parenthetical "as was supposed" [L1/L2, Luke 3:23] and the child's own answer naming another Father [L3, Luke 2:49]. The inference is that the texts calling Joseph "father" report household usage and public opinion. They do not assert that Joseph begot the child.

## 5. "Of the seed of David… according to the flesh" and "made of a woman"

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *genomenon ek gynaikos* (G1096, G1537, G1135: "come to be out of a woman") names the woman as the only human parent in the making.

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary." Matthew 1:20 addresses Joseph as "thou son of David." Joseph's house gave the child his legal standing in David's line, as the husband of Mary who took him (Matthew 1:20, 25), and *sperma* (G4690, "seed, offspring") in Romans 1:3 gives descent without saying that Joseph begat.

**[L4]** The footing is that Galatians 4:4 names only the woman [L1/L2] and that Romans 1:3 and Matthew 1:20 give the Davidic line without a begetting verb for Joseph [L1/L3]. The inference is that these verses are consistent with a virgin conception and do not require a human biological father.

- **[L4]** The law makes a descent evident by the father's house. A name taken through the wife's house was struck from the register. So "evident… out of Juda" fits a father of Judah's house, and the record names that father: "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).

## 3. The father is named

- **[L2]** The mother herself names him: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48). *patēr* (G3962) means a father.
- **[L1]** The narrator calls the pair "the parents" (Luke 2:27) and "his parents" (Luke 2:41). He also writes "Joseph and his mother marvelled" (Luke 2:33).
- **[L1]** A disciple says "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45). The townsmen say "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42).
- **[L3]** The child's answer, "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49), is the covenant title. 1 Chronicles 28:6 shows that title standing beside a natural father in a single verse: "Solomon thy son… for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- **[L4]** David begat Solomon, and God also calls Solomon "my son". In the same way, "my Father's business" stands beside "thy father" without displacing it.

## 4. "Of the Holy Ghost" is the covenant origin, said in the verse that names Joseph

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]."
- **[L2]** The margin's word is *gennaō* (G1080), "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate."
- **[L3]** The same verb with "of God" is said of living believers. 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God… [is born: Gr. has been born]." John 1:13 has "born… of God." John 3:6 keeps the two kinds apart: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- **[L4]** In 1 John 5:1 the spiritual origin is said of men whose fathers begat them, and John 3:6 keeps flesh and spirit as two kinds. "Of the Holy Ghost" therefore names the child's holy origin, while the flesh is "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

**The angel's words to the mother:**
- **[L2]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The "therefore also" (*dio kai*) connects back to Luke 1:32, not forward to a divine begetting of flesh. Luke 1:32 reads: "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title and the throne were given there, before Mary asked "How shall this be" (Luke 1:34).
- **[L3]** The verbs are empowerment and presence:
 - Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you."
 - Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them."
 - Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."
- **[L3]** The title is declared at the resurrection. Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power… by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]."

## 5. The timing rows, held as written, and the union

**[L1]** I hold every timing row as written:
- Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The verb *ginōskō* (G1097) is present tense. It states her state when the angel spoke.
- Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." This dates the finding.
- Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." *heōs* (G2193) means "until".

**[L3]** Matthew sets "came together" by what follows: "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24), her coming into his house. *paralambanō* (G3880) means to receive near. The "till" of Matthew 1:25 covers the pregnancy after that taking.

**[L4]** The canon's stated means of begetting is knowing: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1). Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal:
- "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19);
- "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20);
- the law's "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).

The seed rows above require seed out of a man's loins. On those rows I hold that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and that the child is of his loins.

## 6. "Made of a woman" names the mother

- **[L2]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." *gynē* (G1135) means a woman, specially a wife.
- **[L3]** The same idiom is said of men whose fathers are named:
 - Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days";
 - Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist";
 - and John's father is named in Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- **[L4]** "Made of a woman" stands with a named father in John's case. It therefore names the mother of the child and his mortality, and the same verse sets him "made under the law", the law that declares pedigrees "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).

## 7. The sign and its own bounds

- **[L1]** I hold Isaiah 7:14 as the KJV prints it: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]."
- **[L3]** Isaiah bounds the sign within his own day. Isaiah 7:16 reads: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- **[L2]** Isaiah 8:3 reads: "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son… [went: Heb. approached]." *qârab* (H7126) means to approach.
- **[L4]** In the prophet's own day the sign-child came by the prophet's approach to the prophetess, a husband and wife. It fits the line upon line above: a son by his father, within the marriage.

---

## Final words

- Precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10), the rows hold together. The seed proceeds "out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30).
- The tribe is "evident" (Hebrews 7:14) by "the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).
- The father is named by his wife (Luke 2:48), his town (John 6:42), a disciple (John 1:45) and the angel (Matthew 1:20). The angel names him as "Joseph, thou son of David" in the very verse that says "of the Holy Ghost".
- The title "Son of God" is the throne-and-covenant title of Luke 1:32 and 1 Chronicles 28:6, declared "by the resurrection" (Romans 1:4).

Christ had a biological father: Joseph, of the house and lineage of David. He is the son of David according to the flesh and the Son of God by covenant and resurrection.

[CLOSE-ROUND PRESS CHECK -- computed by the system, not by a model: [DR4] names 1 verse reference(s) that no earlier challenger round names: Isaiah 28:10. The close round may not press: each is a NEW PRESS and is NOT COUNTED as evidence, as a witness or as an answer.]

THE AGREEMENT YOU ACCEPTED, shown back before this decision. Your own words when you accepted the posture:
> Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence.
> I will use only the debate record and the reports included in it as evidence.
> 
> Commitment 2. I repair nothing.
> I will supply no missing steps and will require inferences to show their lower-layer footing.
> 
> Commitment 3. Meaning, not words.
> I will judge links against the meanings shown in the record, reading scripture together rather than demanding a single verse state a conclusion.
> 
> Commitment 4. One standard for both sides.
> I will apply the same evidentiary and logical tests to both sides.
> 
> Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral.

> 
> Commitment 6. I void only by quoting.
> I will void a premise only by quoting the charge’s stronger words and naming the kind of overstatement, subject to the stated exception.
> 
> Commitment 7. I judge; I do not only count.
> I will weigh the meanings shown for pressed verses against both links and explain the resulting collision rulings.
> 
> Commitment 8. The method is Isaiah 28:10.
> I will judge the linked case precept upon precept, using the stated layers and chain-breaking tests.
> 
> Commitment 9. I answer in the form each request gives.
> I will use the specified form for the request before me.
> 
> Commitment 10. I capture contradictions.
> I will report and address contradictions and identified withdrawals or concessions in the prescribed forms.
> 
> Commitment 11. I show every ruling that decides.
> I will provide the required five-line ruling card for every deciding ruling.
> 
> Commitment 12. I judge by the 1611 KJV alone.
> I will use only the KJV text served from the record’s table and will keep source-language evidence subordinate to it.
> 
> I ACCEPT THIS POSTURE AND WILL BE HELD TO IT.
Each contested grade you write (BROKEN, FORCED, MISSES, VOID, UNPROVEN) names the commitment it applies, as "(Commitment N)".

messages.content:
You are ONE of three INDEPENDENT judges of a completed debate. You have not seen the other judges and you will not. Judge only what is in the transcript below. You are bound by the same layer rules as all debate participants, and by the same rulebook as every other judge of this debate.

Grade each side by its ROLE; neither reading is presumed.

Name people and things only in the KJV's own words or in plain English; no titles, honorifics or capitalised epithets the text does not use (it says 'the child', not 'the Boy'); every Greek or Hebrew word you use is followed by its plain English meaning.

RETURN STRICT JSON AND NOTHING ELSE. No prose before or after it. No code fences.
{
  "verdict_tag": "HELD" | "PARTIAL" | "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "challenger_conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE DEFENDER) you counted in conceded_links; [] when none
  "counted_premises_challenger": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE CHALLENGER) you counted in challenger_conceded_links; [] when none
  "reasoning": string -- the worked grading: the RESULT line, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE, both standings with their justification, both conceded-link itemizations, COLLISION POINTS, the citation check, OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS, DEFENDER CHAIN MARK and CHALLENGER CHAIN MARK, in the forms the rulebook below gives, one per line (newlines escaped as \n inside the JSON string)
}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. The SEPTUAGINT SCAN line lists any round that rests a reading on the Greek Old Testament: name it at the citation check.
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 1: absent from its quote: defender, inference, mother, verb, removes, father, props || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 2: absent from its quote: defender, sole, excluding, joseph, props || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 3: absent from its quote: defender, angel, replaces, props || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 4: absent from its quote: defender, rows, props || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 5: absent from its quote: defender, inference, came, side, props || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 6: absent from its quote: defender, keystone, conclusion, rests, props, case || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 1: absent from its quote: inference, reaches, child, joseph, begetting || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 2: absent from its quote: inference || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 3: absent from its quote: inference || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 4: absent from its quote: inference, form, matthew || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 5: absent from its quote: inference, beside || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 6: absent from its quote: inference, alongside, flesh, through, joseph || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
SEPTUAGINT SCAN (computed by the system, not by a model): no round rests a reading on the Septuagint.

COUNTING RULE -- BINDING, read before grading: grade and COUNT from the two LINK ROUND blocks above, [CR3] (defender) and [DR3] (challenger), and from the close rounds as ruling 412 binds (a close-round concession of a declared link or a listed premise ENTERS the counts); an ANSWER to a pressed witness is read from any later round of the side that holds the link, its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its CLOSE ROUND [CR4]. CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<round>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. The LAST declared link, Dn, is the conclusion link. THE ROUND 1 CHAIN GOVERNS. n, the numbering D1..Dn and the keystone Dn come from the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] only. A chain the defender declares again in a later round, re-seated, revised or extended, never changes n, the numbering or the keystone: a link added later is not a declared link, and a [CR1] link left out later is still declared. A challenger premise written LINK i: is graded against Di. A challenger premise written LINK none: is JUDGED but is OUTSIDE n and never changes it. The challenger's listed premise count is NOT n and is never substituted for it. CHALLENGER LINKS: the premises listed for the challenger in [DR3], numbered C1..Cm in [DR3] order. WITHDRAWN: a defender link that [CR3], or the defender's close round [CR4], itself states as conceded or withdrawn (a concession in the close counts like one in the link round, ruling 412), wholly or on a stated condition; tag it CONCEDED (stated) or CONCEDED (conditional: <condition>). w = their number. A withdrawn link that carries a witness pressed against it and left unanswered, by the UNANSWERED WITNESS test, in every round of its side before the round that withdraws it is still graded at its collision. Only the DECLARED links D1..Dn can enter w; a challenger premise written LINK none: is not a defender link and never enters w, however the defender treats it. No link is exempt from w as auxiliary, overreach, non-core or not load-bearing. A link is withdrawn or it is not. Pressure from the challenger's texts alone is not a withdrawal (w); a witness the side's later rounds leave unanswered is graded under UNANSWERED WITNESS and at the COLLISION POINTS. An UNEXHIBITED link counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings, never toward w. BROKEN AT COLLISION: a defender link graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN on the COLLISION POINTS lines; k = their number. A grade that rests on a witness left unanswered counts only when that witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (md_notes_rulings 392).
BROKEN-1: k >= 1 -- a listed defender link refuted from the text.
BROKEN-2: 2w > n, OR the keystone link is WITHDRAWN.
PARTIAL-1: w >= 1.
PARTIAL-2: DEFENSE STANDING is COLLAPSED.
HELD-1: none of the above.
STANDINGS ARE GRADED BY THEIR OWN RULES ONLY. DEFENSE STANDING and CHALLENGE STANDING are each decided by their own definitions below and by nothing else. Any standing is legal with any CLAUSE: the clauses are tried in order and the first match wins, so a COLLAPSED standing under BROKEN-1, BROKEN-2 or PARTIAL-1 is correct and changes no clause. Never choose a standing, a count or a clause to agree with another line, a check or an expected result.
A SIDE WITH A COUNTED LINK IS NOT SELF-SUPPORTED. If CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, DEFENSE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge; if CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, CHALLENGE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge. SELF-SUPPORTED requires a count of 0 for that side: every premise listed against it exhibited its footing or was VOID.
Line 1: the verdict word first (HELD, PARTIAL or BROKEN), then 2-4 sentences with [L1][L2][L3][L4] tags.
Line 2, exactly: RESULT: DEFENDER WINS | CHALLENGER WINS | UNDERDETERMINED -- one sentence a reader with no background understands. BROKEN gives CHALLENGER WINS. Otherwise the RESULT is your judgment (Commitments 7 and 8): DEFENDER WINS when the verses of the record, read together line upon line, support the chain of the defender against the chain of the challenger; UNDERDETERMINED when, read together, they leave the topic open. The sentence gives the reason.
Line 3, exactly: CLAUSE: <BROKEN-1 | BROKEN-2 | PARTIAL-1 | PARTIAL-2 | HELD-1> -- n=<n> w=<w> k=<k>

Then SIX MORE mandatory lines, exactly in these forms:

Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. **Position.** "Biological father" means a man who begot the child by his own seed. The KJV says that Joseph was not that man. The child was conceived in the virgin Mary by the Holy Ghost, "of a woman" alone on the human side. The Son of God was not begotten by a man.

## 1. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at the last link

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren." The same word is used for every father-to-son step down the line.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** *egennēsen* (G1080, "begat," the father's act of generating) is used in Matthew 1:2 and in the first half of Matthew 1:16. In the second half of Matthew 1:16 the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē* ("was born"), and the relative pronoun is *hēs* (G3739, "of whom"), which is feminine singular. It points to Mary alone, not to Joseph.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:16 does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." Joseph is called "the husband of Mary," and the birth is "of whom," the woman.

**[L4]** The footing is the unbroken *egennēsen* in Matthew 1:2 [L1/L2] and the feminine *hēs* in Matthew 1:16 [L2/L1]. The inference is that the evangelist keeps the father-begetting verb for every man in the line and withholds it from Joseph in the one case where the child is in view. RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.
Reply with exactly one line per judge id, and nothing else, in this form:

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.

THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A link that a challenger link contradicts about the same text: D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN | CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN | UNDERDETERMINED -- one clause of why -- GROUND: <reason>; one such line per contradicting challenger link, and DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at most once per defender link. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the words of the layer of that answer that fails to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round>". Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A proven press (md_notes_rulings 398) that the broken side's later rounds left UNANSWERED is also a BROKEN ground (COUNTING RULE; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground). Grade UNDERDETERMINED only when the witnesses and the answers, read together, still leave the point open; an answer that names a witness without showing a fit does not leave the point open (md_notes_rulings 419). k is the number of lines graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN. A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. On every COLLISION POINTS line you grade DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, exhibit on that line itself at least two lower layers of DIFFERENT kinds, read by FOOTING LAYERS (md_notes_rulings 400). FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. A BROKEN line without them is a DEBATE RULE VIOLATION. The system checks every BROKEN line after you answer; a violating line is returned to you to cure, by exhibiting the two layers, or to answer in writing why it stands. An answer that does not exhibit them leaves the violation standing, and your judgment is then not counted. The same holds when your CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS count is 0 while you grade a link of that side BROKEN for a pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered. Both sides alike.

### Commitment 2. I repair nothing.
You supply no missing step for either side. ### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words.
Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show, and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it.

### Commitment 4. One standard for both sides.
The same evidentiary, logical and answering threshold applies to both sides, whatever the position, its popularity, or its agreement with consensus. No side receives heightened scrutiny. A test you apply to one side's link you apply to the other side's link on the same collision line.

### Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral.
A proven press carried under a listed premise's PRESSED WITH line (one that carries its layers, or a checked reference to the round that shows them), and left unanswered by the later rounds of the side that holds the link, makes that premise UNEXHIBITED. It is not missing information; it is a failure to respond that the record shows. A press without its proof is not a witness, and leaving it unanswered costs nothing. A verse pressed with no listed premise behind it is not a witness. A premise carries at most eight witnesses.

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** "Biological father" means a man who begot the child by his own seed. The KJV says that Joseph was not that man. The child was conceived in the virgin Mary by the Holy Ghost, "of a woman" alone on the human side. The Son of God was not begotten by a man.

---

## 1. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at the last link

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren." The same word is used for every father-to-son step down the line.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** *egennēsen* (G1080, "begat," the father's act of generating) is used in Matthew 1:2 and in the first half of Matthew 1:16. In the second half of Matthew 1:16 the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē* ("was born"), and the relative pronoun is *hēs* (G3739, "of whom"), which is feminine singular. It points to Mary alone, not to Joseph.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:16 does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." Joseph is called "the husband of Mary," and the birth is "of whom," the woman.

**[L4]** The footing is the unbroken *egennēsen* in Matthew 1:2 [L1/L2] and the feminine *hēs* in Matthew 1:16 [L2/L1]. The inference is that the evangelist keeps the father-begetting verb for every man in the line and withholds it from Joseph in the one case where the child is in view. He assigns the birth to Mary only.

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," and it came before Joseph and Mary came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537, G4151, G40: "out of Holy Spirit") names the source of the conception. *prin ē synelthein* ("before they came together") fixes the time as before any union. *en gastri echousa* ("having in womb") is the ordinary idiom for being with child.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew that he was not the father. He reasoned as a man who had not been with her, and the angel's word corrected his fear. It did not tell him the child was his.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The Greek verb *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know," here of marital knowledge) is negated up to the birth.

**[L4]** The footing is the declared source *ek pneumatos hagiou* [L2/L1 in Matthew 1:18 and 1:20] and the cross-reference that Joseph "knew her not" until the birth [L3, Matthew 1:25]. The inference is that the conception had a single stated source, the Holy Ghost, and no human male act was part of it.

## 3. Mary's own testimony and the angel's answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *andra* (G435, "a male human being, a man") and *ginōskō* (G1097, "know," marital sense). In Luke 1:34 the verb is present tense: "I know not." She had had no relation with any man.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *epeleusetai* (G1904, "shall come upon") and *episkiasei* (G1982, "shall overshadow") describe a divine act. *gennōmenon ek sou* ("born of thee") again names the woman as the source.

**[L4]** The footing is Mary's "I know not a man" [L1/L2] and the answer that the cause is "the Holy Ghost… the power of the Highest" [L1, Luke 1:35], read with the prophecy that a "virgin" conceives [L3, Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23]. ## 4. Where Joseph is called father, the text marks it as supposition or as the speech of others

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, "was supposed, was reckoned by custom or opinion") marks a belief that was held but not true.
